answer: At dawn, the protocol aggregates cryptographic evidence of coordinated equivocation across bonded identities: each implicated pair contributes a slash, so k colluding identities incur a penalty proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²). Detection also triggers an exponential capital-loss multiplier as swarm size grows, amplified by asymmetric depreciation of remaining collateral in the vault. Splitting stake among sybils therefore increases correlated exposure rather than diluting the cost; violet-tagged identities receive no exemption.
